title: Dream of the Red Chamber
blurb: Dream of the Red Chamber — the fourth and last of the Four Great Classical Novels in this library. The Jia family's decline told through the love triangle of Baoyu, Daiyu, and Baochai.
background: Honglou Meng (Dream of the Red Chamber, also titled 石头记 / The Story of the Stone) is one of the Four Great Classical Novels of Chinese literature, and by critical consensus the greatest of them. It was composed by Cao Xueqin (曹雪芹, c. 1715–1763) in the last decades of his life; the first 80 chapters circulate as his, and the last 40 were completed and published by Gao E (高鹗) in the 1791 printed edition. The novel follows the decline of the aristocratic Jia family (贾) through the love triangle of the heir Baoyu (宝玉) with his fragile, poetic cousin Daiyu (黛玉) and his poised, worldly cousin Baochai (宝钗), set against the daily life, rituals, poetry, and politics of a great Beijing household. Where the other three Great Novels are driven by history, myth, or brotherhood, Honglou Meng is the great Chinese novel of interiority: it is read as a meditation on illusion and reality (色/空), on the cost of literary civilization, and on the unstoppable decay of a once-great family. Cao wrote in a register that fuses classical prose, vernacular dialogue, and hundreds of original poems, lyrics, riddles, and opera texts in the voices of his characters — no other Chinese novel rewards close line-by-line reading the way this one does, which is precisely why it belongs in this library. Of the Four Great Novels it is the only one placed in tier A, matching its canonical standing.
